To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of an ABA/abiotic stress-inducible promoter in the CBF1 transgenic tomato plants improved tolerance to abiotic stresses without affecting growth or yield.
the ABRC1-CBF1 tomato plants showed enhanced tolerance to chilling and salt stress without affecting growth and yield under control conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of transgenic crops that are tolerant to biotic and abiotic stresses, and which maintain normal growth and yield under non-stressed conditions.
the improvement of the agronomic performance of transgenic tomato plants under stress and normal conditions by the use of an ABA/stresses induced promoter.
the development and characterization of transgenic tomato plants with improved abiotic stress tolerance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of ABRC1- ABA-responsive complex 1 promoter to drive the Arabidopsis DREB1A gene in tomato improves tolerance to chilling, drought and salt stress without affecting yield.

the use of the ABA/stress responsive promoter ABRC1 to drive CBF1 expression in tomato plants resulted in enhanced abiotic stress tolerance without any negative impact on plant growth and yield under non-stressed conditions.

the use of ABRC1- ABA-inducible promoter in tomato plants expressing the Arabidopsis cold- regulated gene CBF1, is a promising approach to enhance tolerance to abiotic stresses without affecting growth and yield.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of the ABRC1 to express Arabidopsis CFB1 in transgenic plants is promising in terms of improving plant stress tolerance without affecting the plant growth and yield under non-stress conditions.

the use of the ABA-responsive complex promoter from the barley HVA22 gene to express Arabidopsis CBI in tomato improved stress tolerance without affecting the growth and yield of the transgenic plant under normal conditions.
we have developed transgenic tomato plants expressing the Arabidopsis DREB1/CBF1 gene under the control of a strong ABA/stress responsive complex ABRC1 promoter from the barley HVA22 gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of an ABRC1 promoter in the expression of Arabi- dopsis CBF1 gene in tomato plants improved the stress tolerance of the transgenic lines without affecting their agronomic performance.
we were able to express CBF1 under a stress inducible promoter and the trans- genic plants were tolerant to the stress conditions without compromising yield.
the use of the ABRC1 promoter to drive CBF1 expression in tomato plants can improve the stress tolerance of tomato plants without affecting yield.
